summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for progressively worsening lower extremity edema, shortness of breath, and generalized leg pain. Evaluation ruled out DVT and pulmonary embolism, with normal cardiac function and low BNP making heart failure unlikely. The edema was attributed to chronic venous insufficiency, obesity, and poor dietary sodium adherence. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli was identified and treated with a short course of ciprofloxacin. Her chronic conditions—HIV, hepatitis B and C, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and osteoarthritis—remained stable. She received physical therapy to address weakness and was transitioned to injectable furosemide for easier management. The patient improved clinically, with reduced swelling and resolved UTI symptoms, and was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation.
